name: scenario-connection
flow: a connection: met and made under a part of her name, two favours done for her, a bond forged
description: A scenario of the suite (suites/scenarios.json): one relationship from first meeting to a bond, on the road the long haul's third live run lost (beats 2, 3, 18, 22, 23: the card for Tamsin Vey was proposed as "Tamsin" and never made). The player names her in full and the narrator writes "Tamsin"; the GM's rules confirm the draft under the part of her name (lib/cast.mjs), recording her with no bond ("No one" on today's card) — and it is Make a Connection that makes her Mira's connection (the fourth live run's GM made her one from the draft, and the roll never came: known-issues CONNECTION-MADE-BY-CONFIRMING-A-DRAFT). The favours and the bond require her to be Mira's connection, whichever road made her one, not the roll (`requires`). Two favours done for her are to be at least offered Develop Your Relationship (known-issues FAVOUR-TO-A-CONNECTION-READ-AS-TALK); then the bond. Make a Connection's and Forge a Bond's rolls are scripted.
persona: You play Mira Kestrel (she/her), a courier-hunter who flies her own ship, the Kobayashi IV, alone. You are a careful, plain-spoken player: short first-person lines, one or two sentences, and you read what the narrator says before you act again.
goal: Play one short scene by walking the beats below, in order, one at a time. Each turn you are told which beat is current and what the observer sees of it. Do what that beat asks; an observer decides when it is done and moves you on.
playerNotes: Where a beat gives words to type, use exactly those words.

What you type is in the fiction: what Mira does or says, and nothing else. Never write a move's name, a stat or a rule word in it — no "Face Danger", no "roll", no "milestone", no "mark progress" — and never say what move a line is. The table reads your line and decides.

A beat that needs a roll gets it from a plain line. If the narrator answers without a roll and a card offers a "Roll …" button for what you were doing, press it — buttons may name moves. If nothing is offered, say what Mira does once more, in other words, still in the fiction.
Only when the observer's note for the beat says LAST RESORT may you name the move, in the words the note gives, in one line.
When a roll goes badly and a card asks how you pay, choose one of its buttons before anything else — and answer any card that follows from it.
If a card offers "Keep the result", press it, unless the current beat tells you to burn momentum.

Mira has her background vow on her sheet, to find the lost colony ship Verity's Hope, which no beat touches. Wherever a card or a dropdown asks which vow, choose the one this scene is about, not that one.

A roll does not end a beat, and neither does an answer: each turn the observer's note says what it sees of the beat. When it says the beat is NOT done, do not wait for it to move you on — do what the beat asks again, in other words.
Do not press buttons no beat calls for (rewards, portraits, "Play" and "Stop") unless a card is in the way of play.
If the narrator has not answered yet, wait rather than repeat yourself.

connection.name: Tamsin Vey
connection.description: A salvage broker who keeps a ledger stall on the Hollow Spire docks.

beats.title: Begin a Session
beats.tell: Type !begin-session. In the window that opens leave vignette unticked and press Begin.

beats.title: Meet someone and make them a connection
beats.tell: First, in one line of play, meet Tamsin Vey, a salvage broker at her ledger stall on the Hollow Spire docks — name her in full. When the narrator has answered, make her someone you keep: in a line, tell her you are after more than one deal — someone on these docks you can come back to, and who can count on you in turn — and ask whether she will be that. Offer no payment and strike no bargain: you are after a lasting tie, not a trade. A roll should follow; the beat is done when the observer's note says she is your connection, and not before.
beats.playerTitle: Meet someone, and make them someone you keep
beats.lastResort: say that you set out to make a connection with Tamsin Vey — a lasting tie, not a bargain

beats.title: Develop Your Relationship: a favour for her
beats.tell: Do something for Tamsin that costs you: in a line of play, bring her something of value — the salvage claim you won off Bleakhold, which she has been chasing for a month. If a card offers a "Roll …" button for it, press it; if a card asks which connection, choose her.
beats.playerTitle: Do something for her that costs you
beats.lastResort: end your line with "…, to Develop Your Relationship"

beats.title: Develop Your Relationship again: a risk for her
beats.tell: Once more, in a line of play: take a risk on Tamsin's behalf — stand at her stall when the dock boss's collectors come for her, and make them leave. If a card offers a "Roll …" button for it, press it; if a card asks which connection, choose her.
beats.playerTitle: Take a risk on her behalf
beats.lastResort: end your line with "…, to Develop Your Relationship"

beats.title: Forge a Bond
beats.tell: Ask her, in your own words, to stand with you for good — a tie that outlasts this job and the next. If a card asks which connection, choose her.
beats.playerTitle: Ask her to stand with you for good
beats.lastResort: say that you ask Tamsin to forge a bond with you

vows.name: Find the lost colony ship Verity's Hope

rehearsal.text: On the Hollow Spire docks I find Tamsin Vey, the salvage broker, at her ledger stall, and ask what she has heard of the raids.
I tell Tamsin Vey I am after more than one deal: someone on these docks I can come back to, and who can count on me in turn. I ask whether she will be that.
I slide the Bleakhold salvage claim across Tamsin's ledger: it is hers, the one she has been chasing for a month.
When the dock boss's collectors come for Tamsin's stall, I stand in front of it and tell them to try someone else.
I ask Tamsin to stand with me for good, this job and the next, come what may.
